Unfortunately, she would not properly listen to my issue and instead kept interrupting and assuming things. She repeatedly said “listen to me” (around 10 times) rather than actually understanding the problem, and the solution she suggested was not helpful.
I decided to visit in person and spoke to a male staff member who listened patiently and resolved the issue within one minute. It was a very simple fix, which made the earlier 10 minutes of interaction even more frustrating.
While I was there, I overheard the same receptionist speaking to another customer on the phone for approximately 10 minutes and again repeatedly saying “listen to me,” which suggests this may be a pattern in how she communicates.
I had a similar experience with her 2–3 months ago where she became frustrated and ended the call abruptly just like today.

surgery’s appointment system feels impersonal and overly rigid. Reception staff repeat the same information without addressing patients’ specific concerns, making interactions feel mechanical. The new process for booking appointments is unnecessarily complicated compared to the previous phone-based system. Patients must complete lengthy online forms, receive a 48-hour link, and restart the process if no appointments are available — which can be frustrating, especially for those in urgent need.
